subject: HealthSys DPA - restriction on use for model training & execution steps
summary: Negotiation of a strict carve-out prohibiting use of customer content for model training; legal redlines and final DocuSign execution link exchanged.
messages:
From: Alice Wong <alice.wong@healthsys.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: HealthSys Procurement <procurements@healthsys.com>
Date: Sun, 9 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA terms - training carve-out request

Hi Camila,

Thanks for sharing the DPA draft. HealthSys has a hard requirement that any customer content (including logs, prompts, and derived artifacts) must not be used to train, improve, or evaluate models outside of our environment. We need an explicit, signed carve-out in the DPA that: 
- Prohibits use of customer content for model training or algorithmic improvement;
- Requires a definition of "customer content" that includes de-identified derivatives and embeddings;
- Requires documentation of all subprocessors that may touch content and a 30-day notice before adding a new subprocessor.

I've attached a PDF with our suggested language (HealthSys_DPA_Redlines.pdf). Can Redwood accept these as non-negotiable for this contract? If not, please point us to the alternatives and the process/timeline for escalations.

Best,
Alice
Alice Wong
Head of Privacy & Compliance, HealthSys
[Attachment: HealthSys_DPA_Redlines.pdf (pdf)]

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@healthsys.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 08:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA terms - training carve-out request

Alice —

Appreciate the clarity and the redlines. Short answer: we understand the requirement and can accommodate a strict carve-out, but we need to align on definitions and subprocessors. Next steps from our side:

1) Loop in legal to validate the precise wording for "customer content" and whether embeddings/derived vectors are included.
2) Confirm subprocessors list and agree on notice cadence (we typically do 30 days for material changes).
3) If the language materially changes our operational model (e.g., disables aggregate offline telemetry), legal will propose narrowly tailored exceptions limited to debugging and security, with explicit opt-in.

I'm putting Marissa (legal) and Rishi (privacy) on copy to propose redline language. Aditya — quick heads-up: HealthSys is a pilot customer; any runtime changes or feature flags we need to avoid?

I'll get back within 24 hours with our suggested DPA redline.

Thanks,
Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Clean_Sig.docx (docx)]

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 11:43:00 -0800
Subject: FW: DPA terms - suggested redlines for HealthSys (internal)

Camila / team — forwarding HealthSys request and my quick take. Key points for negotiation: 

- Definition scope: propose wording that covers "Customer Content" = all content uploaded, generated, or derived from customer inputs including de-identified derivatives and embeddings. This matches HealthSys ask and is defensible.
- Training carve-out: we can accept a prohibition on using Customer Content for model training or improving models that are shared outside the customer's tenancy. We should include a security/bug-fix exception: limited, time-boxed, and anonymized, with customer consent for any use beyond debugging.
- Subprocessors: we already maintain a living list; commit to 30-day notice for additions and an option for customers to object. For core infra (cloud provider) we cannot practically give a veto but will provide compensating controls (contractual commitments, SOC2).
- Auditability: offer quarterly summary of data-handling activities and the ability to request an audit under MFA scheduling.

I've drafted redline language and attached it (HealthSys_DPA_Redlines_RedwoodComments.pdf). If HealthSys accepts these, we can push the DocuSign envelope for signature.

Marissa
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: HealthSys_DPA_Redlines_RedwoodComments.pdf (pdf)]

From: HealthSys Procurement <procurements@healthsys.com>
To: camila.reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA terms - training carve-out request

On Wed, Nov 12, 2025 at 11:43 AM marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Camila / team — forwarding HealthSys request and my quick take. Key points for negotiation:
>
> - Definition scope: propose wording that covers "Customer Content" = all content uploaded, generated, or derived from customer inputs including de-identified derivatives and embeddings.
>
Thanks Marissa — the proposed language looks acceptable to legal. We have two small asks before we sign: 

1) Add an explicit sentence that "Customer Content will not be used to train, improve, or evaluate machine learning models accessible beyond the customer's dedicated environment, unless explicit written consent is obtained."
2) Provide the current subprocessor list and confirm 30-day notice process in writing.

If you can confirm both, please send the final DPA on DocuSign. We have procurement approval pending the signed DPA.

--
Procurement Ops, HealthSys
